title: Remarks by Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent Before the EXIM Annual Conference
summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent delivered a policy speech at the EXIM Annual Conference emphasizing economic security as a pillar of national security, highlighting supply chain vulnerabilities in critical sectors (semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, energy) and touting Administration initiatives including the Critical Minerals Strategic Reserve (Project Vault). The speech cited Iran tensions in the Strait of Hormuz (~20% of global energy supply transit) as an example of how supply chain resilience has become essential to withstanding geopolitical shocks.
key_points: Iran's recent actions in the Strait of Hormuz threaten approximately 20% of global daily energy supply, highlighting supply chain chokepoints as a macro risk factor
EU imported a record 57% of its liquefied natural gas from the US in 2025; Asian nations signed over $56 billion in new US energy deals in 2025
Project Vault (US Critical Minerals Strategic Reserve) launched in February 2026, with EXIM financing unlocking $12 billion for critical-minerals procurement including ~$2 billion in private equity
Taiwan still produces 90% of the world's highest-value chips, leaving semiconductor supply chains highly concentrated and vulnerable
Up to 90% of US medicines and active pharmaceutical ingredients come from India and China, creating pharmaceutical supply chain dependencies
The Administration frames this as a shift toward 'economic statecraft' aligning public and private capital to reinforce national power and supply chain resilience
Semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, and advanced manufacturing/AI are identified as key sectors requiring supply chain resilience work
why_it_matters: The speech articulates a coherent policy framework around supply chain security and economic statecraft that could inform future trade, investment, and industrial policy decisions. For markets, the explicit linking of supply chain resilience to national security signals potential ongoing policy support for domestic manufacturing, energy exports, and critical minerals—all of which carry implications for commodity markets, trading relationships, and sectoral capital allocation.
macro_context: The speech describes a macro environment where geopolitical tensions (Iran in Strait of Hormuz) create supply chain shocks, but states that US energy abundance policies have helped the economy withstand these shocks. The framing suggests that supply chain resilience in energy, critical minerals, semiconductors, and pharmaceuticals is now a central macroeconomic variable alongside conventional military capability.
